```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r open}
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
```

The examples use invented data. `nis` is a query over Parquet files. DuckDB
reads the columns needed when you ask for a result.

| Task | Where the work happens |
| --- | --- |
| `select()`, `filter()`, code flags, and derived outcomes on an open query | Add steps to the DuckDB query. |
| `nis_attrition()`, coding audits, `nis_cell_counts()`, and supported `nis_survey()` summaries | Aggregate in DuckDB and return the result to R. |
| `nis_design()` | Collect the cohort columns and sampled hospital structure needed for an R survey design. |
| `collect()` | Bring the rows and columns in the query into R. |
| `nis_suppress()` on a data frame or survey table | Work on an object already in R. |

## Define the domain after identifying the sample

A cohort is the set of discharges that meet your study criteria. A survey domain
is the subpopulation you estimate within the original sample design. In the next
example, both designs estimate the same cohort total. Filtering the input first
changes the standard error and design degrees of freedom.

```{r filter}
domain <- nis_design(nis, cohort = heart_failure, keep = AGE)
filtered <- nis_design(filter(nis, heart_failure), cohort = TRUE, keep = AGE)
bind_rows(full_sample = summarise(domain, total = survey_total()),
          prefiltered = summarise(filtered, total = survey_total()), .id = "design")
c(full_sample = survey::degf(domain), prefiltered = survey::degf(filtered))
```

`filter()` on the open query removes discharges before the design is defined.
Pass eligibility to `nis_design(cohort = )` or use `filter()` on an existing
`nis_design()` or `nis_survey()` object to define a domain within the sample.
Hospital-years with no eligible cases still contribute zero to the variance
calculation. See [How the NIS survey design works](nis-design.html).

## Choose a survey object

| Your analysis | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A cohort fits in R and you want srvyr, survey, or gtsummary methods. | [`nis_design()`](../reference/nis_design.html) |
| You need to analyze many discharges and your summary or model has a DuckDB-backed method. | [`nis_survey()`](../reference/nis_survey.html) |

## Decide how to pool years

The original discharge weights estimate totals across the included years.
`annualize = TRUE` divides every weight by the number of included design years.
This rescales a pooled total to an average per included year and leaves means,
proportions, and odds ratios unchanged. Each partial year counts as one year.
See [Years and coding eras](years-and-eras.html) for coverage checks.

## Document how you handle singleton strata

A lonely primary sampling unit (PSU) is the sole sampled hospital in a
stratum. `survey.lonely.psu` sets the variance policy for those strata.
`survey.adjust.domain.lonely` controls adjustments for a single contributing
hospital in a domain within a stratum that has multiple sampled hospitals.
Choose and report the settings used in your study.
